questions.title: ASCII Byte Average Calculator
questions.description:
An encoding inspector computes the average ASCII code of the characters in a string. Read a line and print the integer average (rounded down via integer division) without using String#bytes or aggregation methods like sum/inject.

Input Format:
A single line of text.

Output Format:
An integer — the floor of the average ASCII code of the characters.

Constraints:
1 <= line length <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def byte_average(line)
  total = 0
  count = 0
  line.each_char do |c|
    total += c.ord
    count += 1
  end
  count == 0 ? 0 : total / count
end

line = gets.chomp
puts byte_average(line)

questions.title: ATM Withdrawal Rescue
questions.description:
An ATM dispenses cash only if the amount does not exceed the balance. Define a custom `InsufficientFundsError` and rescue it.

Input Format:
Line 1: float balance. Line 2: float amount.

Output Format:

Constraints:
0.0 <= balance, amount <= 100000.0.

A bank ledger tool processes n transactions. Each transaction line is either "deposit <amount>" or "withdraw <amount>" where amount is a float string. Starting balance is 0.0. Print the final balance to 2 decimals using a while loop (iterators and sum are disabled).

questions.title: Bank Account Multi Operation Statement
questions.description:
An `Account` class stores `@balance` and a `@transactions` array (both set in `initialize`). Instance methods `deposit(amount)` and `withdraw(amount)` mutate both. The `statement` method prints `Balance: <bal>`, `Transactions: <count>`, and the comma-joined transaction labels (only if any). Read initial balance, then n, then n `deposit X` or `withdraw X` commands.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer balance. Line 2: integer n. Next n lines: `deposit X` or `withdraw X`.

Output Format:
Two or three lines from `statement`.

Constraints:
0 <= balance, amounts <= 1000000; 0 <= n <= 100.
questions.whitelist: def initialize, def deposit, def withdraw, def statement
questions.sourcecode:
class Account
  def initialize(balance)
    @balance = balance
    @transactions = []
  end
  def deposit(amount)
    @balance += amount
    @transactions << "+#{amount}"
  end
  def withdraw(amount)
    @balance -= amount
    @transactions << "-#{amount}"
  end
  def statement
    puts "Balance: #{@balance}"
    puts "Transactions: #{@transactions.length}"
    puts @transactions.join(",") if @transactions.any?
  end
end
bal = gets.to_i
acct = Account.new(bal)
n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  op, amt = gets.split
  if op == "deposit"
    acct.deposit(amt.to_i)
  elsif op == "withdraw"
    acct.withdraw(amt.to_i)
  end
end
acct.statement

questions.title: Bank Branch Counter With Subclasses
questions.description:
A bank tracks accounts across account types. Define a Bank base class with @@accounts and @@total_balance starting at 0. The constructor takes a balance and increments both class variables. Define class methods self.accounts, self.total_balance, and self.average (returns 0 when @@accounts is 0, otherwise integer division). Define Savings and Checking subclasses whose constructors call super(balance). Read n then n lines 'type balance' (type is S for savings, C for checking); print three lines: 'Accounts: <n>', 'Total: <total>', 'Avg: <avg>'.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'type balance' (type in S, C).

Output Format:
Three lines as described.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 100; 0 <= balance <= 1000000.
questions.sourcecode:
class Bank
  @@accounts = 0
  @@total_balance = 0
  def initialize(balance); @balance = balance; @@accounts += 1; @@total_balance += balance; end
  def self.accounts; @@accounts; end
  def self.total_balance; @@total_balance; end
  def self.average; @@accounts.zero? ? 0 : @@total_balance / @@accounts; end
end

class Savings < Bank
  def initialize(balance); super(balance); end
  def type; "Savings"; end
end

class Checking < Bank
  def initialize(balance); super(balance); end
  def type; "Checking"; end
end

n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  parts = gets.split
  kind = parts[0]
  bal = parts[1].to_i
  if kind == "S"
    Savings.new(bal)
  else
    Checking.new(bal)
  end
end
puts "Accounts: #{Bank.accounts}"
puts "Total: #{Bank.total_balance}"
puts "Avg: #{Bank.average}"

questions.title: Bank Withdrawal Ampersand Block
questions.description:
An ATM withdrawal method takes a balance, an amount, and an `&block` authorizer. If the block returns true and amount <= balance, deduct and report OK; if amount exceeds balance, report INSUFFICIENT; if the block returns false, report DENIED.

Input Format:

  if block.call
    if amount <= balance
      [balance - amount, "OK"]
    else
      [balance, "INSUFFICIENT"]
    end
  else
    [balance, "DENIED"]
  end
end

questions.title: Banking Namespace Taxable Audit
questions.description:
A banking system nests modules: `Banking::Accounts` contains module `Taxable` (10 percent tax instance method `tax_amount`) and module `Auditable` (class method `audit(amount)`). The `Savings` class includes `Taxable` and extends `Auditable`. Read an initial balance, create `Banking::Accounts::Savings.new(balance)`, then print the total (balance plus tax) followed by `Banking::Accounts::Savings.audit(total)`.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer balance.

Output Format:
Two lines: the integer total, then `AUDIT: <total>`.

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 1000000.
questions.whitelist: module Banking, module Accounts, include Taxable, extend Auditable
questions.sourcecode:
module Banking
  module Accounts
    module Taxable
      def tax_amount
        (@balance * 10) / 100
      end
    end
    module Auditable
      def audit(amount)
        "AUDIT: #{amount}"
      end
    end
    class Savings
      include Taxable
      extend Auditable
      def initialize(balance)
        @balance = balance
      end
      def total
        @balance + tax_amount
      end
    end
  end
end

questions.title: Benchmark Loop Versus Formula
questions.description:
Compute the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n two ways: (a) using a manual loop timed by Benchmark.measure; (b) using the closed-form formula n*(n+1)/2 timed by another Benchmark.measure. Compare both results and print "match" if they are equal, otherwise "mismatch".

Input Format:

Output Format:
The single word "match" or "mismatch".

formula_total = n * (n + 1) / 2
Benchmark.measure { formula_total = n * (n + 1) / 2 }
puts loop_total == formula_total ? "match" : "mismatch"

questions.title: Binary Representation Builder
questions.description:
Convert a non-negative integer to its binary representation (as a string of 0/1, most-significant bit first) using a while loop. The built-in to_s with base argument is disabled.

Input Format:
A single non-negative integer.

Output Format:
A single line containing the binary representation (no leading zeros, except for input 0 which prints "0").

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 10^9.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
if n == 0
  puts "0"
else
  bits = []
  m = n
  while m > 0
    bits << (m % 2)
    m = m / 2
  end
  out = ""
  i = bits.length - 1
  while i >= 0
    out += "#{bits[i]}"
    i -= 1
  end
  puts out
end

questions.title: Caesar Cipher Encoder
questions.description:

def shift(c, k)
  if c >= "a" && c <= "z"
    base = "a".ord
    n = c.ord - base
    n = (n + k) % 26
    (base + n).chr
  elsif c >= "A" && c <= "Z"
    base = "A".ord
    n = c.ord - base
    n = (n + k) % 26
    (base + n).chr
  else
    c
  end
end

questions.title: Concurrent Bank Account Ledger
questions.description:
A bank account starts with balance 100. Read n transactions, each 'deposit X' or 'withdraw X'. Two teller threads split the transaction list in half; each computes its net change (deposits positive, withdrawals negative) and applies it to the shared balance under a mutex.     op, amt = txns[i][0], txns[i][1].to_i
    bal += amt if op == "deposit"
    bal -= amt if op == "withdraw"
  end
  mutex.synchronize { balance += bal }
end
t2 = Thread.new do
  bal = 0
  (half...n).each do |i|
    op, amt = txns[i][0], txns[i][1].to_i
    bal += amt if op == "deposit"

end

questions.title: Dynamic Finder With Method Missing
questions.description:
A record finder supports dynamic find_by_X-style lookups via method_missing. Records are stored in a frozen DATA constant. method_missing handles names starting with 'find_' by extracting the field after the prefix and returning the id of the first matching record or 'not found'. Read n then n lines 'field:value'; for each, dispatch 'find_<field>' via send and print the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'field:value'.

Output Format:
One result per line (id string or 'not found').

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= field, value length <= 20.
questions.sourcecode:
class Finder
  DATA = [
    { "id" => "1", "name" => "Alice", "city" => "NYC" },
    { "id" => "2", "name" => "Bob", "city" => "LA" },
    { "id" => "3", "name" => "Carol", "city" => "NYC" }
  ].freeze
  def method_missing(name, *args)
    n = name.to_s
    if n.start_with?("find_")
      field = n[5..]
      row = DATA.find { |r| r[field] == args[0] }
      row ? row["id"] : "not found"
    else
      super
    end
  end
end

f = Finder.new
n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  line = gets.chomp
  field, value = line.split(":")
  puts f.send("find_#{field}", value)
end

questions.title: Enumerable Reading Log Stats
questions.description:
A sensor readings aggregator class `ReadingLog` mixes in `Enumerable` and exposes `each`. Read n then n integer readings. Compute the total, the highest reading, and the count manually by iterating with `each`. Print three lines: `Total: X`, `Top: Y`, `Count: Z`.

Output Format:
Three lines as described.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -10000 <= reading <= 10000.

class ReadingLog
  include Enumerable
  def initialize(vals) @vals = vals end
  def each
    @vals.each { |v| yield v }
  end
end

vals = n.times.map { gets.to_i }

questions.title: Enumerable Temperature Log Spread
questions.description:
A weather station stores daily temperatures in `TempLog` which mixes in `Enumerable` with a custom `each`. Read n then n float readings. Compute the average and the spread (highest minus lowest) manually by iterating with `each`. Print two lines: `Avg: X.XX` and `Spread: Y.YY`.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: one float reading each.

Output Format:
Two lines with two-decimal floats.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -1000.0 <= reading <= 1000.0.
questions.sourcecode:
class TempLog
  include Enumerable
  def initialize(readings) @readings = readings end
  def each
    @readings.each { |r| yield r }
  end
end
n = gets.to_i
readings = n.times.map { gets.to_f }
log = TempLog.new(readings)
total = 0.0
lo = readings.first
hi = readings.first
log.each do |r|
  total += r
  lo = r if r < lo
  hi = r if r > hi
end
avg = total / n
puts "Avg: #{'%.2f' % avg}"
puts "Spread: #{'%.2f' % (hi - lo)}"

questions.title: Exclusive Range Interval Intersector
questions.description:
A scheduler computes the overlap of two time windows represented as exclusive integer ranges (a...b) and (c...d). Read four integers and print the integers that fall in both ranges, space-separated, in ascending order. Iterate the first range with each and test membership in the second range using include?; do not use Set, intersection, & or union.

Input Format:
A single line containing four space-separated integers a, b, c and d.

Space-separated integers in the intersection (ascending). If the intersection is empty, print nothing (the test cases always have a non-empty intersection).

def intersect(a, b, c, d)
  result = []
  (a...b).each do |x|
    if (c...d).include?(x)
      result << x
    end
  end
  result
end

questions.title: Fiber Collatz Sequence Generator
questions.description:
Read a positive integer n. Use a Fiber that yields successive values of the Collatz sequence starting from n: if x is even, next is x/2; if odd (and > 1), next is 3*x+1; stops at 1. Resume the fiber repeatedly and print each yielded value on its own line.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.

Output Format:
One value per line, the full Collatz sequence from n down to 1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
f = Fiber.new do
  x = n
  loop do
    Fiber.yield x
    break if x == 1
    x = x.even? ? x / 2 : 3 * x + 1
  end
end
loop do
  v = f.resume
  break if v.nil?
  puts v
end

  while count < n

    a, b = b, a + b

end

questions.title: Fiber Number Generator
questions.description:
Read an integer n. Use a Fiber that yields the integers 1, 2, ..., n one at a time. Resume the fiber repeatedly and print each yielded value on its own line.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.

Output Format:
n lines, each containing one integer from 1 to n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
f = Fiber.new do
  i = 1
  while i <= n
    Fiber.yield i
    i += 1
  end
end
loop do
  v = f.resume
  break if v.nil?
  puts v
end

questions.title: Fibonacci Method With Memo Hash
questions.description:
Define a method fib(n, memo = {}) that returns the n-th Fibonacci number where fib(1) = 1, fib(2) = 1, fib(3) = 2, and so on. Use early return for n <= 2, and memoize using the hash argument. Read n and print fib(n). Do not use while, until, or for.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single integer, the n-th Fibonacci number.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 30
questions.sourcecode:
def fib(n, memo = {})
  return 1 if n <= 2
  return memo[n] if memo.key?(n)
  memo[n] = fib(n - 1, memo) + fib(n - 2, memo)
end
n = gets.to_i
puts fib(n)

questions.title: File Line and Char Tally
questions.description:
A text-mining tool needs the number of lines and total characters (excluding newlines) in a document. Read n lines, write them to a file, then use `File.foreach` to count lines and characters, printing `LINES: X CHARS: Y`.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: any non-empty text.

Output Format:
`LINES: X CHARS: Y` with X=n and Y=total non-newline chars.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; each line length 1..80.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
lines = n.times.map { gets.chomp }
path = "/tmp/atom_ruby_tally.txt"
File.open(path, "w") { |f| lines.each { |l| f.puts l } }
line_count = 0
char_count = 0
File.foreach(path) do |l|
  line_count += 1
  char_count += l.chomp.length
end
puts "LINES: #{line_count} CHARS: #{char_count}"

questions.title: Filter Hash Above Threshold
questions.description:
Given a hash of items with integer quantities, keep only entries whose quantity is strictly greater than a threshold. Print remaining entries sorted by key. Implement filtering manually with each; the select, filter, reject and keep_if methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: item name and integer quantity separated by a space.
Last line: integer threshold.

Output Format:
One line per remaining item (sorted alphabetically): '<item> <qty>'.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= item length <= 20, 0 <= quantity <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
def keep_above(pairs, threshold)
  result = {}
  pairs.each do |k, v|
    result[k] = v if v > threshold
  end
  result
end

n = gets.to_i
pairs = []
n.times do
  k, v = gets.split
  pairs << [k, v.to_i]
end
threshold = gets.to_i

kept = keep_above(pairs, threshold)
kept.keys.sort.each do |k|
  puts "#{k} #{kept[k]}"
end

questions.title: Filter Lambda Strict Arity

Constraints:

n.times { nums << gets.to_i }
threshold = gets.to_i
keep = lambda { |x| x > threshold }
result = nums.select(&keep)
puts result.join(" ")

questions.title: First Multiple Of Seven With Break
questions.description:
Read n followed by n space-separated integers. Print the first value in the list that is a multiple of 7, or -1 if no such value exists. Use the each iterator and the break keyword to stop early. Do not use find, detect, select, or first.

Input Format:
First line: integer n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single integer, the first multiple of 7 found, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -10000 <= value <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
arr = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
result = -1
arr.each do |x|
  if x % 7 == 0
    result = x
    break
  end
end
puts result

questions.title: Fiscal Calendar Quarter and Peak
questions.description:
Given a month (1..12) and day, compute the calendar quarter (1..4), fiscal half ("H1" for months 1..6, "H2" otherwise), and whether the month is in peak season (months 6..8 or month 12). Use the range operator and case-equality only.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers month day.

Output Format:
Single line: "Qx Hx peak|off".

Constraints:
1 <= month <= 12, 1 <= day <= 31
questions.blacklist: case, when, if, elsif, else, unless, between?, cover?
questions.sourcecode:
month, day = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
quarter = (1..3) === month ? 1 :
           (4..6) === month ? 2 :
           (7..9) === month ? 3 : 4
half = (1..6) === month ? "H1" : "H2"
peak = ((6..8) === month || month == 12) ? "peak" : "off"
puts "Q#{quarter} #{half} #{peak}"

questions.title: FizzBuzz One To N With For In
questions.description:
Print the FizzBuzz sequence from 1 to n using a for in loop. Multiples of 3 print "Fizz", of 5 print "Buzz", of both 15 print "FizzBuzz", otherwise print the number. Do not use each, map, times, or step.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
n lines, one entry per line, following FizzBuzz rules.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
for i in 1..n
  if i % 15 == 0
    puts "FizzBuzz"
  elsif i % 3 == 0
    puts "Fizz"
  elsif i % 5 == 0
    puts "Buzz"
  else
    puts i
  end
end

questions.title: Grade with Honors Classification
questions.description:
Given a numeric score and attendance percentage, determine the final classification. If attendance is below 75%, the student fails. Otherwise grade by score: 90..100 = A (but A+ if attendance >= 95), 80..89 = B, 70..79 = C, otherwise F. Use nested control structures combining if/elsif and case/when.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: score attendance.

Output Format:
Single line: "fail", "A+", "A", "B", "C", or "F".

Constraints:
0 <= score <= 100, 0 <= attendance <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
score, att = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
if att < 75
  puts "fail"
else
  grade = case score
  when 90..100
    if att >= 95
      "A+"
    else
      "A"
    end
  when 80..89
    "B"
  when 70..79
    "C"
  else
    "F"
  end
  puts grade
end

questions.title: Greet If Block Given
questions.description:
Define a method `greet(name)` that checks `block_given?`. If a block is supplied, yield the name to it; otherwise print `Hi there`.

Input Format:

Output Format:
Either `Hi NAME` or `Hi there`.

Constraints:
Name length 1..30; flag is 0 or 1.
questions.sourcecode:
def greet(name)
  if block_given?
    yield name
  else
    puts "Hi there"
  end
end

name = gets.chomp
flag = gets.to_i
if flag == 1
  greet(name) { |n| puts "Hi #{n}" }
else
  greet(name)
end

A warehouse tracks item quantities in a hash. Read N entries (item name and integer quantity on each line). Read a query item and print its quantity, or 0 if the item is not stocked.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: an item name and an integer quantity separated by a space.
Last line: the query item.

Output Format:
A single integer: the quantity, or 0 if the item is not stocked.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= item length <= 20, 0 <= quantity <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
stock = {}
n.times do
  item, qty = gets.split
  stock[item] = qty.to_i
end
query = gets.chomp
puts stock.fetch(query, 0)

questions.title: Inventory Validation Raise
questions.description:
A warehouse log records items as `name qty`. Validate each entry: qty must be 0..1000. Use custom exception classes; rescue and aggregate the valid/invalid lists.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: `name qty` separated by space.

Output Format:
Line 1: comma-separated `name:qty` of valid items. Line 2: comma-separated error messages for invalid items.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; -1000 <= qty <= 10000; name length 1..20.
questions.sourcecode:
class InvalidQuantityError < StandardError; end
class InvalidNameError < StandardError; end

n = gets.to_i
valid = []
invalid = []
n.times do
  line = gets.chomp
  parts = line.split
  name = parts[0]
  qty = parts[1].to_i
  begin
    raise InvalidNameError, "Bad name: #{name}" if name.nil? || name.empty?
    raise InvalidQuantityError, "Bad qty: #{qty}" if qty < 0 || qty > 1000
    valid << "#{name}:#{qty}"
  rescue InvalidNameError, InvalidQuantityError => e
    invalid << e.message
  end
end
puts valid.join(", ")
puts invalid.join(", ")

questions.title: Inventory Value Calculator
questions.description:
A warehouse tool reads n inventory items, each line: name qty price (qty integer, price float). Compute total inventory value (sum of qty * price) and the number of bulk items (qty > 10). Higher-order iterators are disabled.

Input Format:
First line: integer n. Following n lines: name qty price (space-separated).

Output Format:
Two lines: total value to 2 decimals, then the count of bulk items.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= name length <= 20, 1 <= qty <= 10000, 0 <= price <= 10^6.
questions.blacklist: each, inject, reduce, sum, map, select
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
total_value = 0.0
bulk_items = 0
i = 0
while i < n
  name, qty, price = gets.split
  q = qty.to_i
  p = price.to_f
  total_value += q * p
  if q > 10
    bulk_items += 1
  end
  i += 1
end
puts "%.2f" % total_value
puts bulk_items

questions.title: Inventory Value Report
questions.description:
Read N categories, each containing M items with quantities. The data is stored as a nested hash {category => {item => qty}}. For each category, compute the total quantity across its items using each, and print 'category total' sorted by category name. The sum, reduce, inject, group_by and select methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: two integers N (number of categories) and M (items per category).
For each category:
  Line 1: category name.
  Next M lines: item name and integer quantity separated by a space.

Output Format:
N lines, each '<category> <total>' sorted alphabetically by category name.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, 1 <= M <= 100, 1 <= name length <= 20, 0 <= quantity <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
def category_totals(records)
  result = {}
  records.each do |cat, items|
    total = 0
    items.each do |_, qty|
      total += qty
    end
    result[cat] = total
  end
  result
end

n, m = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
records = {}
n.times do
  cat = gets.chomp
  items = {}
  m.times do
    name, qty = gets.split
    items[name] = qty.to_i
  end
  records[cat] = items
end

totals = category_totals(records)
totals.keys.sort.each do |c|
  puts "#{c} #{totals[c]}"
end

questions.title: Inventory self Empty Factory
questions.description:
An `Inventory` class stores `@items` (hash) set in `initialize`. The class method `self.empty` returns a new instance. The instance method `add(name, qty)` accumulates quantities; `total` returns the sum. Read n then n `name qty` pairs. Use `Inventory.empty` to construct, then print the total quantity.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: `name qty` separated by space.

Output Format:
The integer total quantity.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; 0 <= qty <= 10000; name length 1..20.
questions.whitelist: def self.empty, def add, def total
questions.sourcecode:
class Inventory
  def initialize
    @items = {}
  end
  def self.empty
    new
  end
  def add(name, qty)
    @items[name] = (@items[name] || 0) + qty
  end
  def total
    t = 0
    @items.each { |name, qty| t += qty }
    t
  end
end
n = gets.to_i
inv = Inventory.empty
n.times do
  name, qty = gets.split
  inv.add(name, qty.to_i)
end
puts inv.total

questions.title: Iterator Builder With Ampersand Block
questions.description:
Build a custom iterator `iterate_all(arr, &block)` that walks the array using a `while` loop and invokes the block via `block.call` for each element. Use it to produce squares of the input integers.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line of space-separated squared integers.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -1000 <= v <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
def iterate_all(arr, &block)
  i = 0
  while i < arr.size
    block.call(arr[i])
    i += 1
  end
  arr
end

raw = gets.split
arr = []
i = 0
while i < raw.size
  arr << raw[i].to_i
  i += 1
end

puts squared.join(" ")

questions.title: JSON Multi-Document Aggregator
questions.description:
Read a target year on line 1, then a JSON array on line 2 of records each {"category":...,"amount":...,"date":"YYYY-MM-DD"}. Parse the JSON with the JSON module, parse each date with Date.new (split on '-'), filter records whose year matches the target, group amounts by category (summing), and print "<category> <total>" lines sorted by category.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer year. Line 2: a JSON array of records.

Output Format:
One line per category (matching the year), sorted by category name.

Constraints:
1 <= array length <= 100; 1 <= amount <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
require "json"
require "date"
year = gets.to_i
raw = gets.chomp
arr = JSON.parse(raw)
groups = {}
arr.each do |item|
  parts = item["date"].split("-").map(&:to_i)
  d = Date.new(parts[0], parts[1], parts[2])
  next unless d.year == year
  cat = item["category"]
  groups[cat] = 0 unless groups.key?(cat)
  groups[cat] += item["amount"]
end
keys = groups.keys.sort
keys.each { |k| puts "#{k} #{groups[k]}" }

questions.title: Library Late Fee Yield
questions.description:
A library charges a fixed daily late fee per overdue book. Implement `compute_fees(records, rate)` that yields each `(book_id, fee)` pair when a block is given, otherwise accumulates. The caller block prints and totals.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: `book_id days` separated by space. Daily rate is 0.50.

Output Format:
N lines `BOOK_ID FEE` (2 decimals), then a final line with the total fee (2 decimals).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 0 <= days <= 365.
questions.sourcecode:
def compute_fees(records, rate)
  results = []
  records.each do |(id, days)|
    fee = days * rate
    if block_given?
      yield id, fee
    else
      results << [id, fee]
    end
  end
  results
end

n = gets.to_i
records = []
n.times do
  parts = gets.split
  records << [parts[0], parts[1].to_i]
end
rate = 0.50
total = 0.0
compute_fees(records, rate) do |id, fee|
  puts "#{id} %.2f" % fee
  total += fee
end
puts "%.2f" % total

questions.title: Library Loan Eligibility Matrix
questions.description:
A library checks loan requests using a matrix. Patrons have a type (student, faculty, guest), a current checked-out count, an overdue flag, and a requested loan duration. Overdue patrons are denied. Otherwise each patron type has a max-books and max-days limit: student (5, 14), faculty (20, 90), guest (2, 7). Deny if current count >= max or requested days > max, otherwise approve. Use modifier if/unless and case/when.

Input Format:
Line 1: patron_type books_checked_out. Line 2: is_overdue requested_days.

Output Format:
Single line: "approved" or "denied".

Constraints:
patron_type in {student, faculty, guest}, 0 <= books_checked_out <= 1000, is_overdue in {0,1}, 1 <= requested_days <= 365
questions.subtopic: Modifier Forms of if and unless
questions.inputconstrains: patron_type in {student, faculty, guest}, 0 <= books_checked_out <= 1000, is_overdue in {0,1}, 1 <= requested_days <= 365
questions.sourcecode:
type, books = gets.split
books = books.to_i
overdue, days = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
max_books, max_days = case type
when "student" then [5, 14]
when "faculty" then [20, 90]
when "guest" then [2, 7]
else [0, 0]
end
status = "denied" if overdue == 1
status = "denied" if !status && books >= max_books
status = "denied" if !status && days > max_days
status = "approved" unless status
puts status

questions.title: Masked Email Printer
questions.description:
A privacy tool masks the local part of an email address so only its first character is visible, followed by three asterisks and the domain. Implement the masking by scanning characters manually with a while loop; do not use regex substitution methods.

Input Format:
A single line containing an email address.

Constraints:
1 <= email length <= 100; email always contains exactly one @ character
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= email length <= 100; email contains exactly one @
questions.sourcecode:
def mask_email(email)
  at_pos = -1
  i = 0
  while i < email.length
    if email[i] == "@"
      at_pos = i
      break
    end
    i += 1
  end
  return email if at_pos == -1
  first = email[0]
  domain = email[at_pos..]
  first + "***" + domain
end

line = gets.chomp
puts mask_email(line)

questions.description:

Records are passed in via the constructor. Read n then n lines 'op field value' (op in find_by, count_by); dispatch '<op>_<field>' via send and print the result.

  end

questions.title: Multi-Step Pipeline With Exception Aggregation
questions.description:
A pipeline applies three steps to each input integer: double it (raise if input negative), add one (raise if doubled result exceeds 1000), then stringify (raise if value is 0). Aggregate successes and failures across all inputs.

class StepError < StandardError
  attr_reader :step, :input
  def initialize(step, input, msg)
    @step = step
    @input = input
    super("Step #{step} failed on #{input}: #{msg}")
  end
end

def step_double(x)
  raise StepError.new("double", x, "negative") if x < 0
  x * 2
end

def step_add_one(x)
  raise StepError.new("add_one", x, "overflow") if x > 1000
  x + 1
end

def step_to_s(x)
  raise StepError.new("to_s", x, "zero") if x == 0
  "Result: #{x}"
end

errors = []
nums.each do |x|
  begin
    r = step_double(x)
    r = step_add_one(r)
    r = step_to_s(r)
    results << r
  rescue StepError => e
    errors << e.message
  end
end
puts results.join("; ")
puts errors.join("; ")

questions.title: Rainwater Harvest Trap
questions.description:
An array of non-negative integers represents the elevation map of a rainwater harvesting trench of width N. Compute how many units of water can be trapped after raining using the two-pointer technique with a while loop. The max, min, sort, reduce and select methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated non-negative integers (heights).

Output Format:
A single integer: total units of trapped water.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= each height <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
def trap_water(heights)
  left = 0
  right = heights.length - 1
  left_bound = 0
  right_bound = 0
  total = 0
  while left <= right
    if heights[left] <= heights[right]
      if heights[left] >= left_bound
        left_bound = heights[left]
      else
        total += left_bound - heights[left]
      end
      left += 1
    else
      if heights[right] >= right_bound
        right_bound = heights[right]
      else
        total += right_bound - heights[right]
      end
      right -= 1
    end
  end
  total
end

questions.title: Range Palindrome Prime Counter
questions.description:
A number theorist counts integers in a range that are both prime and palindromic (read the same forwards and backwards). Read two integers a and b and iterate the inclusive range with each. Implement primality and palindrome checks manually with while loops; do not use Prime, prime?, select or count.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
An integer — the number of palindrome primes in a..b.

Constraints:
1 <= a <= b <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
def is_prime(n)
  return false if n < 2
  i = 2
  while i * i <= n
    return false if n % i == 0
    i += 1
  end
  true
end

def is_palindrome(n)
  s = n.to_s
  i = 0
  while i < s.length / 2
    if s[i] != s[s.length - 1 - i]
      return false
    end
    i += 1
  end
  true
end

def count_palindrome_primes(a, b)
  count = 0
  (a..b).each do |n|
    if is_prime(n) && is_palindrome(n)
      count += 1
    end
  end
  count
end

questions.title: Record Find By With Respond To Override
questions.description:
A record class supports dynamic find_by_<field> queries via method_missing, and overrides respond_to? to report true for any find_by_ name. The frozen DATA constant holds three records. method_missing returns the comma-joined ids of all matching records, or 'none' if no match. Read n then n lines 'field:value'; for each, dispatch 'find_by_<field>' via send and print the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'field:value'.

Output Format:
One result per line: comma-joined ids or 'none'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= field, value length <= 20.
questions.sourcecode:
class Record
  DATA = [
    { "id" => "1", "name" => "Alice", "age" => "30" },
    { "id" => "2", "name" => "Bob", "age" => "25" },
    { "id" => "3", "name" => "Carol", "age" => "30" }
  ].freeze

  def respond_to?(name)
    n = name.to_s
    n.start_with?("find_by_") ? true : super
  end

  def method_missing(name, *args)
    n = name.to_s
    if n.start_with?("find_by_")
      field = n.sub("find_by_", "")
      matches = DATA.select { |r| r[field] == args[0] }
      matches.empty? ? "none" : matches.map { |r| r["id"] }.join(",")
    else
      super
    end
  end
end

r = Record.new
n = gets.to_i

  line = gets.chomp
  field, value = line.split(":")
  puts r.send("find_by_#{field}", value)
end

questions.title: Sort Hash by Value Descending
questions.description:
Given a hash of products and sales counts, print them sorted by sales count descending, breaking ties by product name ascending. Implement sorting with a while loop (bubble sort). The sort, sort_by, max and min methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: product name and integer sales count separated by a space.

Output Format:
N lines, each '<product> <sales>' ordered by sales descending (ties by product ascending).

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, 1 <= product length <= 20, 0 <= sales <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
def rank_by_value(pairs)
  n = pairs.length
  swapped = true
  while swapped
    swapped = false
    (n - 1).times do |i|
      a, b = pairs[i], pairs[i + 1]
      should_swap = false
      if a[1] < b[1]
        should_swap = true
      elsif a[1] == b[1] && a[0] > b[0]
        should_swap = true
      end
      if should_swap
        pairs[i], pairs[i + 1] = pairs[i + 1], pairs[i]
        swapped = true
      end
    end
  end
  pairs
end

n = gets.to_i
pairs = []
n.times do
  p, v = gets.split
  pairs << [p, v.to_i]

  cheapest = prices[0]

    cheapest = p if p < cheapest

def top_k_finishers(times, k)
  pairs = []

    swapped = false

        swapped = true
      end
    end
  end
  k.times do |i|
    t, idx = pairs[i]
    puts "#{idx + 1} #{t}"

questions.title: Word Frequency Reporter
questions.description:
A word analytics tool reads a sentence and prints each distinct word (lowercased) together with how many times it occurs, sorted by count descending then alphabetically ascending. Implement counting manually with a hash; do not use tally, group_by, count or inject.

Input Format:
A single line containing words separated by single spaces.

Output Format:
One line per distinct word in the form "<word> <count>", sorted as described.

Constraints:
1 <= line length <= 500
questions.sourcecode:
def gather_words(line)
  counts = {}
  word = ""
  line.each_char do |c|
    if c == " "
      unless word.empty?
        counts[word] = (counts[word] || 0) + 1
        word = ""
      end
    else
      word += c.downcase
    end
  end
  unless word.empty?
    counts[word] = (counts[word] || 0) + 1
  end
  counts
end

line = gets.chomp
counts = gather_words(line)
result = counts.map { |k, v| [k, v] }.sort do |a, b|
  if a[1] == b[1]
    a[0] <=> b[0]
  else
    b[1] <=> a[1]
  end
end
result.each do |w, n|
  puts "#{w} #{n}"
end
